thread:
Jon: FYI I hit a confusing bundler + edge error while onboarding a customer sample app. Repro is small but the failure mode mixes auth retry behavior and a CJS/ESM resolution bug.
Ellen: oof, that sounds messy. Can you paste the minimal steps and error?
Jon: Minimal repro steps:
```
# clone
git clone https://example.com/rw-sample-edge-auth-repro.git
cd rw-sample-edge-auth-repro
npm ci
# build with vite (prod) and deploy to Vercel Edge emulator
npm run build && vercel dev --edge
```
Jon: App code (server entry):
```
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference';
import { setupAuth } from './auth';

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
await client.generate('ping');
```
Jon: On local Node (dev) this works. After Vite production build + deploy to Edge emulator I get `ReferenceError: require is not defined` or sometimes `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor` depending on bundler flags. Bundle logs show vite/rollup preferring the CJS path for resolution: "preferring 'main' for redwood-inference -> node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.cjs".
Tomas: Do you use any auth middleware that conditionally imports types or does retries? Sometimes dynamic imports or conditional require for retry helpers trigger different code paths and make bundler pick CJS.
Jon: The auth helper does a tiny dynamic import for a retry backoff util: `const backoff = await import('retry-utils');` But the weird bit is if the bundler inlines a small shim the SDK ends up resolved wrong.
Zoe: Could be two separate issues colliding: (1) resolver mainFields picking CJS; (2) default vs named export interop; (3) edge runtime not supporting require. All make sense. Any package.json exports in SDK?
Jon: SDK package.json has: "exports": { ".": { "import": "dist/index.mjs", "require": "dist/index.cjs" } }, "sideEffects": false. ESM entry is default export class.
Ellen: `sideEffects: false` + types-only imports or conditional dynamic imports can confuse tree-shakers. If bundler thinks only types are used or something is tree-shaken, the minifier can remove what looks unused. That can change symptoms by build flags.
Tomas: Quick repro tips: 1) run vite build with `--sourcemap` and inspect vendor chunk to see which file it resolved. 2) run `node --input-type=module dist/bundle.js` locally to reproduce runtime without deploying.
Zoe: For immediate workaround in sample app: force resolver to prefer ESM by adding to vite.config.js: `resolve: { mainFields: ['module','main'] }` and pin @rollup/plugin-node-resolve with same option. Also change consumer code to `import * as RW from 'redwood-inference'; const Client = RW.default || RW;` as a temporary guard. Ugly but works.
Ellen: Long term SDK fixes we should discuss: - publish `exports.browser` -> points to `dist/index.browser.mjs` so bundlers targeting web/edge pick ESM browser build - add a stable named export `export function createClient(opts){ return new Redwood(opts) }` so consumers can `import { createClient }` which avoids default interop - avoid `sideEffects: false` (or whitelist the entry) so bundlers don't accidentally tree-shake runtime - include `module` and `browser` fields in package.json for older bundlers - add a small CI matrix that builds a sample app with vite/rollup/webpack and runs the built bundle under node --input-type=module and a lightweight edge emulator to catch `require is not defined` regressions.
Jon: Also add a note in onboarding sample README about bundler pitfalls and auth/retry dynamic imports. I hit this while trying to show customers the built-in retry on 401 -> it masked as a bundler issue which was confusing.
Tomas: We should also add a minimal example in examples/edge that uses Vite with recommended config and verifies auth retry behavior in CI (so onboarding customers have a working template).
ci-bot: Build job bundle-check failed on branch fix/export-named: `ReferenceError: require is not defined` https://ci.example.com/9987
Zoe: I'll open an SDK issue with the minimal repro, build logs, and suggested packaging changes. Jon, can you attach the sample repo and the failing vendor chunk snippet?
Jon: Done, opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 with repro and logs, assigned to @pkg-maintainers and @eng-devex. I'll follow up with a PR that adds `createClient` + `exports.browser` + CI bundle smoke tests.
Ellen: Nice. For immediate docs, I'll add a short troubleshooting section to the SDK README and the sample app README with the Vite/webpack/rollup snippets.
Jon: Thanks all — I'll post PR link here once ready.
